about.title: Rio Dell Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Rio Dell is a small town, but the traffic moving through it isn't. US-101 SB, the SR-283 Eagle Prairie Bridge, and the stretch of US-101 near Davis Street all see steady collision activity, and even a town this size can have a crash change everything for a family overnight. Public records show injury collisions do happen here, often clustering on Saturday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. when local and through traffic mix. Whether you were hit near Blue Slide Road, on the bridge, or coming off the highway, the moments after a wreck matter. Insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness memories fades faster than most people expect. We handle car accident cases on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Rio Dell Residents Choose Us

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like Humboldt County or Caltrans — is involved. Talking to us early helps make sure that deadline isn't missed.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash. We can help make sure your share of fault is argued fairly rather than accepted at face value.

items.title: No Cap Doesn't Mean No Fight
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, but insurers still push back hard. It helps to have someone in your corner before you say anything on a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurers often use those statements to find ways to minimize or deny your claim. We can talk to the insurer on your behalf instead.

items.question: What if my crash happened on US-101 or the SR-283 bridge near Rio Dell?
items.answer: Crashes on highway corridors like US-101 SB or the Eagle Prairie Bridge often involve higher speeds and can bring in state agencies like Caltrans, which affects your filing deadlines. Our team is familiar with Humboldt County roads and can help sort out who's responsible and how much time you have.

items.question: Does it cost anything to contact you about my case?
items.answer: No, contacting us is free. We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation.
